sections.overview: Australoheros facetus is a southern South American cichlid native to Uruguay, northeastern Argentina and adjoining river systems, and the type species of its genus.
sections.identification: It has a deep body, usually dark vertical bars and a projecting lower jaw with an upturned mouth; these characters help separate it from close congeners.
sections.habitat: The species occupies freshwater streams, rivers, swamps and lakes across tributaries of the lower Paraná and Uruguay drainages and Uruguayan coastal rivers.
sections.diet: It is a diurnal opportunist that eats detritus and plant matter as well as small aquatic animals, including small fish when available.
sections.behavior: Pairs become territorial while breeding, select exposed stones or wood for egg laying, and both adults guard eggs, larvae and young fish.
sections.reproduction: This substrate-spawning cichlid attaches its eggs to a hard surface; parental defence continues after hatching, with reported guarding of juveniles for one to three weeks.
sections.ecology: Its genus contains many regional look-alikes, including A. scitulus and A. tembe; modern morphological and genetic work emphasizes careful separation of these southern cichlids.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment classifies A. facetus as Least Concern, while the species is non-native and regulated as invasive in parts of Europe.
